The authors train a multimodal DeepHit neural survival model; the UNI2-h ViT is only a frozen, pretrained feature extractor.
Pretrained MolFormer-XL, MolT5 and ESM-2 encoders (BERT-size transformer encoders) are combined with trained MLP projectors (GELU, LayerNorm).
UniZyme builds an attention-based enzyme/substrate encoder with distance and energy biases on attention scores, using small ESM-2 (35M) residue features.
Q-PART uses an R3D convolutional backbone and a convolutional decoder plus Neural CDEs for the aperiodic dynamics.
EPS/AWR are applied to ResNets and MobileNetV2, EfficientFormer/MobileViT and MambaOut, which the text calls CNN, ViT and Mamba models.
StructEvo uses an ESM-2-initialised encoder with cross-attention fusion, a fine-tuned transformer-based ProSST proxy and a CNN proxy.
MS-UDG uses an encoder with a projection head, two MLP modules and a reconstruction decoder; no other family is named.
PyHealth 2.0 implements 25+ models, and its sequence processors are built for recurrent and attention-based models.
MFC uses a ResNet18 CNN feature extractor and multiscale large-kernel convolutions; no other family is named.
NEURONA is a lightweight CNN for fMRI features plus a linear classifier; the VLM only builds the dataset scene graphs.
SonoGym trains PPO agents with a CNN encoder, ACT (a transformer CVAE) and Diffusion Policy agents, and uses a GAN for learning-based ultrasound simulation.
MetaOptimize is tested on a simple two-layer CNN and ResNet-18; the family of the 15M TinyStories language model is not named.
MM-Lego merges SNN (MLP) and attention-based MIL encoders through cross-attention LegoBlocks; ResNet50 is only a pretrained patch encoder.
SIL-C fits K-means and Gaussian prototype memories on top of neural skill decoders and policies trained on GPUs.
WMSE is used to train models across several architectures, but this text does not say which model families the authors trained.
NICER is a nonparametric point-process prototype model fitted on frozen UNI features, and a transformer layer predictor is trained downstream.
DPGS is applied to ABMIL (attention-pooling MIL) and TransMIL (transformer), among other MIL models.
Images are generated with Stable Diffusion 3.5 and Flux.1-dev, and Qwen2-VL produces the captions used as prompts.
The benchmark baselines are a linear model, a one-layer MLP on handcrafted features, EEGNet and TimeConv-CNN; no transformer is named.
